newsitem.title: USA: AT&T chairman says he won't resign - report.
newsitem.headline: AT&T chairman says he won't resign - report.

text.p: AT&T Corp chairman Robert Allen said he is not about to leave the company.

Allen told Business Week magazine that AT&T has not reached a crisis that would force him out, despite a third quarter forecast that fell below Wall Street expectations, which led to a drop in the stock price.
"I have no plans to retire at this time," Allen told Business Week. "The board is not asking me to leave."
AT&T's directors are supporting Allen, the article said.
Allen has scheduled his retirement in the year 2000, but president Alex Mandl's departure has changed things.

The article said Allen might be willing to step aside ahead of that schedule after a transition period if the right candidate to takeover the company is found. The article, headlined "AT&T: Will the bad news ever end" quoted analysts as saying the market has a lack of confidence in the company.

Also, executives close to the company are saying AT&T needs a a new management style and that more risk taking needs to be encouraged. The article highlights some of AT&T's abandoned forays into other businesses such software and computers, new forms of competition from cable and local phone companies and the Mandl's departure.
